questions.q: At any instant the velocity of a particle of mass $500g$ is~\left(2t\overset{^}{i} + 3t^{2}\overset{^}{j}\right)ms^{- 1}$ . If the force acting on the particle at $t = 1s$~is~$( \overset{^}{i} + x\overset{^}{j} ) N$~. Then the value of $x$ will be:$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The equation for velocity is&

$\overset{→}{v} = \left(2t\overset{^}{i} + 3t^{2}\overset{^}{j}\right)$

Thus, the acceleration is~

$\overset{→}{a} = $\dfrac{d\overset{→}{v}}{dt} = \dfrac{d ( 2t\overset{^}{i} + 3t^{2}\overset{^}{j} )}{dt} = \left(2\overset{^}{i} + 6t\overset{^}{j}\right)$

At~$t = 1s$,~$\overset{→}{a} = 2\overset{^}{i} + 6\overset{^}{j}$

The force is written as~$\overset{→}{F} = m\overset{→}{a} = $\dfrac{2\overset{^}{i} + 6\overset{^}{j}}{2} = \overset{^}{i} +$3\overset{^}{j}$

Comparing it with the given value of force,~$x = 3$.

$

questions.q: For a free body diagram shown in the figure, the four forces are applied in the '$x$' and '$y$' directions. What additional force must be applied and at what angle with positive $x$-axis so that the net acceleration of body is zero?
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let additional force required be& $\overset{→}{F}$.

Vector sum of the four forces and additional force.

$\overset{→}{F} + 5\overset{^}{i} - 6\overset{^}{i} + 7\overset{^}{j} - 8\overset{^}{j} = 0$

Force required to make net acceleration~zero

$\overset{→}{F} = \overset{^}{i} + \overset{^}{j}$

Therefore, the required force is~\left|\overset{→}{F}\right| = \sqrt{{1}^{2} + {1}^{2}} = \sqrt{2}N$

Angle with~$x$-axis:~$tan\theta = \dfrac{ycomponent}{xcomponent} = \dfrac{1}{1}$

Thus,~$\theta = 45 °$

$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement (I) : The limiting force of static friction depends on the area of contact and independent of materials.
Statement (II) : The limiting force of kinetic friction is independent of the area of contact and depends on materials.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The limiting force of static friction depends on both the normal force and the coefficient of static friction, but it does not depend on the area of contact.

The force of kinetic friction is indeed dependent on the nature of the materials in contact and the normal force, but not on the area of contact.

Hence, Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

questions.q: A body of mass $200g$~is tied to a spring of spring constant~$12 . 5Nm^{- 1}$,~while the other end of spring is fixed at point $O$. If the body moves about $O$ in a circular path on a smooth horizontal surface with constant angular speed $5rads^{- 1}$, then the ratio of extension in the spring to its natural length will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let the extension in spring be& $x$~and~the natural length of spring be~$l$.

Here the centrifugal force will stretch~the spring.

So, centrifugal force=spring force

$kx = m\left(l + x\right){ω}^{2} ⇒ 12 . 5x = \dfrac{1}{5}\left(l + x\right)25 ⇒ 1 . 5x = l ⇒ \dfrac{x}{l} = \dfrac{1}{1 . 5} = \dfrac{2}{3}$

$⇒ x: l = 2: 3$

questions.q: A ball is thrown upward with an initial velocity ${V}_{0}$ from the surface of the earth. The motion of the ball is affected by a drag force equal to $m\gammav^{2}$ (where $m$ is mass of the ball, $v$ is its instantaneous velocity and $\gamma$ is a constant). Time taken by the ball to rise to its zenith is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Net force on ball,
$F = - mg - m\gammav^{2}$
$a = - g - \gammav^{2}$
$\dfrac{dv}{dt} = - g - \gammav^{2}$
$\mathop{∫}_{v = {V}_{0}}^{v = 0}\dfrac{dv}{g + \gammav^{2}} =\mathop{∫}_{t = 0}^{t}- dt$
${\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{g\gamma}}\tan^{- 1}\sqrt{\dfrac{\gamma}{g}}v\right)}_{v = {V}_{0}}^{v = 0} = - t$
$∴ t = \dfrac{1}{\gammag}\tan^{- 1} \left(\sqrt{\dfrac{γ}{g}}{V}_{0}\right)

$

questions.q: A car is moving on a horizontal curved road with radius $50m$. The approximate maximum speed of car will be, if friction between tyres and road is $0 . 34$. [Take $g = 10ms^{- 2}$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For a car moving with uniform speed along a circular track, the centripetal acceleration is provided by the frictional force acting radially inwards. Therefore, applying Newton's second law along radial direction,

$\mumg = \dfrac{mv^{2}}{r}$

$⇒ v = \sqrt{\murg}$

$= \sqrt{0 . 34 \times 50 \times 10}$

~ $\approx 13ms^{- 1}$

questions.q: A small block of mass $100g$~is tied to a spring of spring constant $7 . 5Nm^{- 1}$ and length $20cm .$ The other end of spring is fixed at a particular point $A .$ If the block moves in a circular path on a smooth horizontal surface with constant angular velocity $5rads^{- 1}$about point $A,$ then tension in the spring is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Centripetal force will be provided by the spring force. Let the elongation in the spring be& $x$, then we can~write

$⇒ kx = m{ω}^{2} ( r + x )$

$⇒ 7 . 5x = 2 . 5 ( 0 . 2 + x )$

$⇒ x = \dfrac{0 . 5}{5} = 0 . 1$

Therefore, required tension will be$T = kx = 0 . 75N$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & a_{\text {sys }}=\left(\frac{m_2-m_1}{m_1+m_2}\right) g=\frac{g}{8} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{m_2}{m_1}=\frac{9}{7}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A block of mass $m$ is placed on a surface having vertical cross section given by $y = \dfrac{x2}{4}$. If coefficient of friction is $0 . 5$, the maximum height above the ground at which block can be placed without slipping is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
At equilibrium, $tan\theta = \mu$.

Now, $tan\theta$ is slope of the curve. Therefore,

$tan\theta = \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x}{2}$

Now,

$\dfrac{x}{2} = 0 . 5 ⇒ x = 1$

Required height

$y = \dfrac{x2}{4} = \dfrac{1}{4}m$.

questions.q: A bag is gently dropped on a conveyor belt moving at a speed of $2ms^{- 1}$. The coefficient of friction between the conveyor belt and bag is $0 . 4$~Initially, the bag slips on the belt before it stops due to friction. The distance travelled by the bag on the belt during slipping motion is : [Take $g = 10ms^{- 2}$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When the bag is dropped on the conveyor belt, the acceleration of the bag will be& $a = \mug = 4ms^{- 2}$

The bag will stop moving on the conveyor when the velocity of the bag and the velocity of the conveyor becomes equal.

$u = 0, v = 2ms^{- 1}$

Using the~equation of motion for constant acceleration,

$v^{2} = u^{2} + 2as$

$⇒ s = 0 . 5m$

questions.q: A string of length $L$ is fixed at one end and carries a mass of $M$ at the other end. The mass makes \left(\frac{3}{\pi}\right)$ rotations per second about the vertical axis passing through end of the string as shown. The tension in the string is $\ldots\ldots$ ML.$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \omega=\frac{3}{\pi} \times 2 \pi=6 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s} \\ & R=L \sin \theta\end{aligned}$
and $T=M \sqrt{g^2+\omega^4 R^2}$ Also, $T \sin \theta=M \omega^2 \cdot L \sin \theta$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad T=M(36) \mathrm{L} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad T=36 \mathrm{ML} \end{aligned}$$

questions.q: A tube of length $50$ cm is filled completely with an incompressible liquid of mass $250g$ and closed at both ends. The tube is then rotated in horizontal plane about one of its ends with a uniform angular velocity $x\sqrt{F}rads^{- 1}$. If $F$~be the force exerted by the liquid at the other end then the value of $x$ will be _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Considering an element of tube of length& $d x$~having mass~$d m$~at a distance of~$x$~from right end as shown in figure below.

Now, force acting of that element is~$F = ∫ \left(d m\right){ω}^{2}x$

Integrating the above relation for whole length of tube, we have~

~$F = {∫}_{0}^{L}\left(\dfrac{m}{L} d x\right){ω}^{2}x$

$= \dfrac{m}{L}{ω}^{2}\dfrac{L2}{2}$~$= \dfrac{m{ω}^{2}L}{2}$

$⇒ \omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{mL}}\sqrt{F}= \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{0 . 25 \times 0 . 5}}\sqrt{F}$

$= \sqrt{16}\sqrt{F}= 4\sqrt{F}rads^{- 1}$

Hence, the value of~$x = 4$.

questions.q: $A person standing on a spring balance inside a stationary lift measures $60$ kg. The weight of that person if the lift descends with uniform downward acceleration of $1 . 8ms^{- 2}$ will be~<u>~ ~ ~ ~ ~ & </u>& $N$.  \left[g = 10ms^{- 2}\right]$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When lift is at rest

$N = mg$

$⇒ 60 \times 10 = 600N$

When lift moves with downward acceleration. In frame of lift pseudo force will be in upward direction.

$N^{'} = M \left(g - a\right)$

$⇒ 60 \left(10 - 1 . 8\right)$

$N^{'} ⇒ 492N$
